previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex history including Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and prior port infections was admitted for persistent fevers, chills, and pelvic pain radiating to her thighs following a course of antibiotics for a presumed UTI. Blood cultures from an outside hospital grew Bacillus species. Initial imaging showed no fistula or bowel obstruction but revealed splenomegaly and a new lung nodule. A pelvic MRI identified a small abscess in the right pectineus muscle, determined to be the source of bacteremia. She was treated with IV vancomycin, completed a course of antibiotics, and became afebrile. Her pain was managed with IV then oral analgesics, and she received IV iron for iron deficiency anemia. Her anticoagulation for SVC syndrome required careful management due to variable coumadin absorption, including a brief bridge with fondaparinux. She had a minor fall with no fracture. She was discharged home on a short course of IV antibiotics, a dilaudid taper, and close follow-up for repeat imaging and blood cultures.
problems: Anticoagulation management in setting of short bowel syndrome

radiology_notes.text:
PORTABLE CHEST ___, 18:47

INDICATION:  NGT placement.

FINDINGS:

The lungs are clear.  CVL is seen with the tip in the SVC and no PTX.  NGT
extends below the diaphragm and its tip is probably in the antrum of the
stomach.

MRI OF THE PELVIS

INDICATION:  Right pectineus abscess with fever and abdominal pain.

___ MRI.

TECHNIQUE:

Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted sequences were performed including dynamic 3D
images acquired prior to, during, and after the uneventful intravenous
administration of 17 cc of Magnevist contrast media.

FINDINGS:

There is continued demonstration of relatively increased signal within the
right pectineus muscle that shows enhancement.  However, the central fluid
collection within has diminished to 3 mm in size.  Overall the entire
inflammatory focus is smaller in size and now measures 1.3 cm in maximum
transverse dimension x 1.5 cm in AP dimension x 2.5 cm in craniocaudad
dimension.  There is no evidence of new inflammation or abscess in the
visualized anatomy.

Incidental finding is that of an 8 mm focus in the region of the right greater
trochanter (series 2, image 24) that is of low signal with respect to
background marrow on non-contrast T2-weighted imaging and demonstrates
enhancement after gadolinium.  The coronal fat sat T2 shows high signal
within.  In retrospect, this was seen on recent CT showing some calcified
matrix within. The constellation of findings is most suggestive of an
enchondroma.  On ___, I will seek a second opinion of Musculoskeletal
specialist in Radiology for further assessment.

Multiplanar reformations, generated and evaluated on an independent
workstation, were essential in delineating the dynamic features in multiple
perspectives.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Diminished size of the inflammatory focus in the right pectineus muscle
with only a tiny residual punctate fluid focus centrally.  No new abscesses or
inflammatory foci.
2.  Incidental finding in the right trochanteric portion of the femur,
probably an enchondroma.
